title: A Punjabi Singer Refused to Marry a Man. Six Days Later, Her Body Was Found in a Canal.
excerpt: Inder Kaur, 29, was abducted at gunpoint in Ludhiana. The accused — a Canada-based permanent resident — allegedly fled back via Nepal. The case has exposed a dark intersection of online relationships, forced marriage, and cross-border impunity.
body:
On the evening of May 13, Punjabi singer and model Inder Kaur, 29, left her home in Ludhiana in a white Ford Figo to buy groceries. She never came back. Six days later, her body was pulled from the Neelo canal in Samrala, triggering a murder investigation that has since gripped Punjab — and drawn uncomfortable attention to the vulnerabilities of women in India’s entertainment industry and the transnational networks that can exploit them.

According to a police complaint filed by her brother, Jotinder Singh, the family had discovered that Inder had been in contact for years with a man named Sukhwinder Singh, alias Sukha — originally from Moga district but now a permanent resident of Canada, where he works in construction. The family alleges that Sukhwinder, along with his father Pritam Singh, a friend named Karamjit Singh, and several unidentified accomplices, kidnapped Inder Kaur at gunpoint with the explicit intention of forcing her into marriage.

An Online Relationship That Turned Lethal

The two had connected through Instagram roughly five years ago. What began as casual online interaction gradually escalated into regular communication. Sukhwinder reportedly visited Inder’s home on multiple occasions and, according to a relative and former municipal councillor Jaspal Singh Giaspura, attended her birthday celebrations earlier this year. He had promised marriage in March but kept delaying.

The breaking point came when Inder Kaur discovered that Sukhwinder was already married with children. She refused to go through with the marriage. The family alleges this refusal triggered a campaign of harassment and threats that culminated in her abduction and murder.

Inder’s brother told investigators that she had spoken to Sukhwinder by phone at approximately 10 PM on May 13, telling him she was heading home. Shortly after, her phone went dead. Her car was recovered a day before her body was found, intensifying the search that led police to the canal.

The Canada Connection

What makes this case particularly disturbing — and relevant beyond Punjab — is the alleged cross-border dimension. The family claims Sukhwinder Singh travelled from Canada to India via Nepal specifically to carry out the crime, and escaped using the same route. If confirmed, this would represent a chilling exploitation of international mobility: a permanent resident of one country allegedly committing premeditated murder in another, then vanishing across borders before police could act.

For the Indian diaspora in Canada, the case raises difficult questions. Canada-Punjab migration corridors are among the most active in the world, and cases involving cross-border harassment, forced marriages, and violence — while still rare — are not unprecedented. The Punjab Police have registered a case and say they are investigating all angles, but the accused remains at large.

A Career Cut Short

Inder Kaur’s biography reads like a story of resilience. Originally from Ludhiana, she had worked as a singer and model, competed in beauty pageants — she won the title of Miss Pune — and appeared in regional films. When the entertainment industry proved financially unstable, she pivoted to makeup artistry and corporate work in Delhi before returning to Ludhiana to rebuild her life.

Her family says she was in the process of refocusing her career and had largely stepped away from the relationships and pressures that came with her earlier public life. That she was targeted precisely when she was trying to move forward makes the crime all the more cruel.

The Larger Pattern

Social media has been flooded with outrage since the news broke, with users demanding strict action and raising broader concerns about the safety of women who become visible through entertainment or social media. The intersection of online grooming, failed romantic expectations, and violence against women is not unique to this case — but the alleged involvement of a Canada-based NRI adds a dimension that law enforcement agencies on both sides of the border will need to address.

Police have confirmed that the body has been sent for post-mortem at the Samrala civil hospital. Further legal sections are expected to be added as forensic evidence develops. Conflicting accounts have emerged — some suggesting Inder may have been travelling with the accused when an argument escalated — but the family maintains this was a planned kidnapping and murder.

Inder Kaur deserved better. The investigation needs to deliver it.
nri_angle: The accused is a Canada-based permanent resident who allegedly exploited international mobility to commit murder and flee via Nepal. The case highlights cross-border vulnerabilities in the Punjab-Canada migration corridor.
author: Diaspora Desk
